evidence_plan.claim: DNA nanostructures can implement logic-gated molecular payload release
evidence_plan.verification: publisher records and Nature Biotechnology reference list

evidence_plan.claim: an intravenously injected DNA origami device delivered thrombin to tumor vessels and inhibited tumors in mice
mobile micro/nanorobot systems require external fields, chemical fuel, or biological propulsion
intravenous nanosystems encounter sequential biological barriers and nonspecific distribution
nanomaterial-containing drug products require product-specific development and characterization
DNA origami can stimulate immune cells depending on sequence and surface design

source_limitations: The reported tumor study is preclinical and does not establish human efficacy.
No general-purpose autonomous self-powered 50-100 nm medical robot is established by these sources.
No new in vivo results are produced in this design-only workflow.
